story.title: The questions that shaped my work

paragraphs.text: My journey into sustainability did not begin with climate policy. It developed through education, real estate practice and experiences that changed the questions I ask about the environments people live and work in.

My mother made education a priority for her children. My own path was not straightforward. I pursued a National Diploma and Higher National Diploma (HND) before earning my B.Tech, later recognising how the distinction between HND and university degree qualifications in Nigeria could affect career opportunities. This taught me to take responsibility for my decisions and to keep going when the way was unclear. At Bells University of Technology, I graduated as the best student in my class with a CGPA of 4.64/5.00.

That journey taught me the value of finding another path when the first is unclear. It also shaped my belief that useful knowledge should be shared. In 2020, I worked with 70 senior secondary students in Asese, Ogun State, sharing study strategies that had helped me academically. The following year, 42 of those students gained university admission.
Another experience changed how I thought about environmental responsibility.

After losing my best friend to drowning at Elegushi Beach in Lagos, I avoided beaches and large bodies of water. In 2025, I returned to the coastline while volunteering at a beach cleanup with The OR Foundation in Accra. Clearing textile and plastic waste while reflecting on nearby Jamestown made environmental issues feel less abstract. I began thinking more deeply about how environmental conditions affect people differently and what responsibility professionals have when their decisions shape those conditions.

Today, I bring those questions into my work in the built environment. My goal is to move beyond addressing inefficiencies after buildings are operational and contribute earlier, when decisions about design, energy, resources and resilience can still be influenced.

education.text: My educational journey taught me that achievement is not always about beginning with the clearest path. After progressing through National Diploma and Higher National Diploma qualifications in Estate Management, I continued to a bachelor's degree and graduated at the top of my class. The experience strengthened my discipline, resourcefulness and willingness to change direction when better information became available.
